artists.biography: William Patrick Corgan, III (born March 17, 1967 in Elk Grove Village, Illinois, U.S.A.), most commonly known as Billy Corgan, is an American vocalist, guitarist, and songwriter best known for his work in the alternative rock band The Smashing Pumpkins (and, briefly, as the frontman for alt-rock supergroup Zwan).  Corgan released his first solo album TheFutureEmbrace on June 21st, 2005. It warranted mostly lukewarm reviews from the press and only sold 69,000 copies. It was followed by a tour of Europe, USA, Australia, and Japan.   Trivia:   The scars on his arms and hands in the artwork for TheFutureEmbrace are his birthmarks.  Corgan is also a huge sports fan.

perplexity.description:
Ogilala is the second solo album by William Patrick Corgan (WPC), released on October 13, 2017, under BMG and Martha's Music. Departing from the alternative rock sound of his work with The Smashing Pumpkins, Ogilala embraces a stripped-down, acoustic-driven style rooted in folk and acoustic rock. The album was co-produced by Corgan and Rick Rubin, featuring minimal instrumentation—primarily acoustic and electric guitars, piano, and Mellotron—with subtle contributions from James Iha and Sierra Swan. The result is an introspective, atmospheric record that highlights Corgan’s songwriting and vocal delivery, with a focus on melody and lyrical depth.

Musically, Ogilala stands apart from Corgan’s previous solo effort, TheFutureEmbrace (2005), which leaned heavily on electronic textures. Instead, Ogilala marks a return to organic arrangements and a more personal, reflective tone. The album’s concise runtime and understated production reflect a deliberate shift toward intimacy and restraint. Upon release, Ogilala received generally favorable reviews, earning a Metascore of 70 based on 16 reviews and a user score of 7.8. Commercially, it reached number 7 on the New Zealand Heatseeker Albums chart and number 86 on the Swiss Albums chart, though it had a more modest showing on the US Billboard 200.
